items.title: Construction Activity Still Above Pre-Pandemic Levels
items.author: Mortgage News Daily
items.content: <article>Residential construction delivered a mixed report in October, with housing starts and completions rebounding while building permits suffered a sizable decline. The biggest concern was single-family permitting, which fell nearly 9% from September, suggesting a weaker pipeline for future construction.  Privately owned housing starts increased  9.9%  to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of  1.309 million , putting them 2.8% above October 2025 levels. Single-family starts rose  4.0%  to  864k , multi-family came in at 433k.  Building permits moved in the opposite direction, falling  7.4%  to an annual rate of  1.295 million . That was also  8.7%  below year-ago levels. Single-family authorizations dropped  8.7%  to  772k , while permits for buildings with five or more units came in at 475k.    The divergence between starts and permits is worth watching. Builders began more projects in October, but the decline in authorizations points to less momentum in the pipeline, particularly for single-family construction.  Completions also rebounded, increasing  6.5%  to an annual rate of  1.272 million . However, that was still  10.4%  below October 2025 levels. Single-family completions rose  6.3%  to  900k , while multi-family completions came in at 362k.</article>

items.title: Mortgage Applications Dip 2.3 Percent as Rates Bounced Back
items.author: Mortgage News Daily
items.content:
<article>Mortgage applications reversed course as mortgage rates moved higher for a second consecutive week. The Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA) reported a  2.3% decline  in total application volume for the week ending November 13, 2026.  Purchase applications led the decline, falling 3% on a seasonally adjusted basis, while refinance applications decreased 2%. On an unadjusted basis, purchase activity was down 7% for the week.      Compared to year-ago levels, purchase applications remained  18% lower , while refinance activity was down  54% . The refinance share of total applications increased to 41.1% from 39.8%, while adjustable-rate mortgage applications accounted for 10.8% of activity.  MBA's Joel Kan attributed the pullback to rising rates. The average 30-year fixed rate in MBA's survey climbed to  7.35% , its highest level in three weeks. Kan also noted that FHA refinance applications increased nearly 7% despite the overall decline in refinance activity, helped by FHA rates running roughly 30 basis points below conforming rates. items.title: Pending Home Sales Hit Another Record Low
items.author: Mortgage News Daily
items.content:
<article>Pending home sales are still testing their lowest levels as contract signings weakened across the country. The National Association of REALTORS® (NAR) Pending Home Sales Index (PHSI), which tracks signed contracts on existing homes, dropped  4.7%  from September and  16.7%  from a year earlier.    October marks the second consecutive month of record-low pending sales. NAR Chief Economist Lawrence Yun suggested  “October could mark the low point in contract signings for this housing cycle, as mortgage rates appear to have topped out,”   Still, the near-term outlook isn't encouraging. Yun warned that two consecutive months of record-low contract signings point to very sluggish fourth-quarter home sales closings, adding "...annual existing-home sales could end up at their lowest level since the mid-1990s, despite the U.S. population having grown by roughly 75 million since then." items.title: Affordability Drives Builder Confidence to 14-Year Lows
items.author: Mortgage News Daily
items.content:
<article>Builder confidence fell to its lowest level in more than 14 years in November, as high mortgage rates, rising construction costs, labor shortages, and hesitant buyers continued to weigh on the housing market. The National Association of Home Builders (NAHB)/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index (HMI) dropped four points to  25 , its lowest reading since April 2012.    All three components declined, current sales conditions took the biggest hit.

  NAHB Chairman Bill Owens cited stepped-up immigration enforcement as a factor keeping legal workers off construction sites, worsening labor shortages and driving up costs. Higher fuel prices are also prompting subcontractors to raise rates, while weak buyer demand is leading some builders to scale back construction.  Builder price incentives climbed to  46%  in November, a new post-Covid high. The average reduction held at  6%  for the eighth consecutive month. Sales incentives were reported by 68% of builders, also a post-Covid high and the 20th consecutive month that at least 60% have offered them.</article>

items.title: Existing-Home Sales Sink to Lowest Level Since 2010
items.author: Mortgage News Daily
items.content:
<article>Existing-home sales had another rough month, and just hit their lowest level since August 2010. Mortgage rates are largely to blame.  The National Association of REALTORS® (NAR) reported a  5.5% monthly decline  and an  8.8% year-over-year decline , bringing the seasonally adjusted annual sales rate to just  3.75 million . Chief Economist Lawrence Yun attributed the weakness to mortgage rates, which have tested levels not seen since 2000.    Inventory continued to improve modestly, even as sales slowed. Total housing inventory reached  1.59 million units , up 1.3% from September and  4.6% year over year,  a  5.1-month supply.  Homes also took slightly longer to sell, with the median time on market increasing to  35 days  from 33 days in September.  Prices continued to rise nationally, although at a much slower pace. Median prices crawled to  $416,700 , up a mere  0.4% from October 2025 . Still, that marked the  40th consecutive month  of year-over-year price gains. The Housing Affordability Index fell to  100.7 , down from 107.3 a year earlier, with affordability deteriorating across the country.   Regional Breakdown (Sales and Prices, October 2026)

items.title: Decent Bounce in Mortgage Demand Thanks to Last Week's Lower Rates
items.author: Mortgage News Daily
items.content: <article>Mortgage applications bounced back in the latest week, with both purchase and refinance activity moving higher. The Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA) reported a  6.2% increase  in total application volume for the week ending November 6, 2026.  NOTE: That Nov 6th date is important as it marked the bottom of the range for interest rates after a nice decline that began in mid October. Rates have risen sharply since then so all that follows is likely a bit of a retrospective. In other words, application demand will probably fall again in next week's data thanks to this week's higher rates.   Purchase applications led the improvement, rising 8% on a seasonally adjusted basis, while refinances increased 5%. Despite the weekly gains, both categories remain well below year-ago levels.      Purchase applications were still  18% below year-ago levels , while refinance activity was down  57% . The refinance share of total applications held steady at 39.8%, while adjustable-rate mortgage applications accounted for 10.9% of activity, down slightly from the previous week.  “The declining trend in rates helped to spur stronger application activity, although the pace of purchase and refinance applications remain considerably lower than a year ago,” said MBA's Joel Kan. FHA and VA purchase applications saw particularly strong gains. The FHA rate fell below 7% for the first time in several weeks, reaching 6.98%, more than 20 basis points below the conforming rate. It is important to note: Kan references the Freddie Mac rate survey here, and real rates have risen materially in the past few days.</article>
